records.name: Philadelphia Martin Luther King Jr. Association for Nonviolence
records.summary: A Philadelphia group that teaches nonviolence and runs family help, including a monthly food distribution and a holiday toy drive for children.
records.what_you_do: Join a nonviolence workshop or a College for Teens session, ask about the monthly food distribution (delivery is available), or apply for the holiday toy drive if your children are unlikely to get toys otherwise.

schedule.text: Food distribution is monthly. The toy drive runs around the holidays. Workshop and class dates are not on the site.

first_step.how: Call 215-751-9300 or use the contact form on philadelphiamlk.org to ask about the monthly food distribution and the next College for Teens session.
first_step.basis: Programs and a monthly food distribution are listed, but the site gives no dates or sign-up steps beyond a contact form and a toy application.

records.notes: Legal name: Philadelphia Martin Luther King Jr Association for Nonviolence Inc. The site has no dated items, so status is probably_active. Footer shows zip 19111, but the site address and the IRS record both point to 19104, so 19104 is used. The Donate button has no destination. No email or social links shown. The yearly awards luncheon and bell ringing are listed without dates.

records.name: Philly Free School
records.summary: A school where students learn at their own pace and help govern it through a direct democracy, with tuition and open houses for families.
records.what_you_do: Families can RSVP for an Open House or fill out the interest form to learn about admissions. The school also rents its space and takes gifts to its annual appeal.

cost.text: Tuition applies. Amounts are on the school's Tuition page, which was not read.

first_step.how: Fill out the interest form on phillyfreeschool.org or RSVP for an Open House.
first_step.basis: The site says how to start: an interest form and Open House RSVPs.

records.notes: Legal name: Philadelphia School of Democracy (aka Philadelphia Free School). This is a tuition school, not a drop-in group. The closest interest tag is youth_leadership, and the owner may want a school tag. Grade levels are not stated on the page read. The site shows a 2025 to 2026 annual appeal but no month, so no last_sign_of_life is written. Blog posts and the events calendar show no dates.

records.name: Philly Autism Kickback
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that holds a yearly Dave & Buster's event and takes donations on its website.
records.what_you_do: Watch the group's social media pages for the next Dave & Buster's event, or give through the Make a Donation page on its website.

schedule.text: Yearly Dave & Buster's event. The one listed was on Nov 22, 2025.

first_step.how: Follow the group on Instagram or Facebook to hear about the next Dave & Buster's event, or use the Make a Donation page.
first_step.basis: The yearly event is public, but registration for the last one was closed and no other way in is listed.

records.notes: Legal name: Philly Autism Kickback Inc (the site writes P. A. K). The site lists one dated item, the Nov 22, 2025 Dave & Buster's event, and no programs, volunteer, or membership information, so this record is thin. The venue is not named on the site, and the IRS address was not published because the site does not show one. The audience is not stated, so no community or crowd tags were added. The category is the closest fit. Owner may want to review before it goes live.

records.name: Righteous Healing Ministries
records.notes: Found only on the IRS record. The website field on the tax form is an email address (righteoushm@gmail.com), recorded as a contact because it carries the group's name, but it is unverified. One search found no web page for this congregation; the hits were other Philadelphia groups and were not used. No services, events, or dates found. The IRS address is 5835 Cedar Avenue, 1st floor, 19143, but no public page confirms it, so it is not written here. Held back until a public page turns up.

records.name: Roboracer Foundation
records.notes: Also known as the F1tenth Foundation (aka on the IRS record). The home page at roboracer.ai returned only its title, so its content is probably loaded by script; /about returned 404. Nothing was readable, so no summary or categories were written. The IRS address is 47 University Mews, Philadelphia 19104, but no page confirms it. Held back. A later pass could try other page paths.

records.name: Sanctuary Fellowship Worship Center
records.summary: A non-denominational, Bible-teaching church on North 42nd Street with women's and men's fellowship groups and outreach that includes clothing giveaways and volunteering at its Safe House Pantry.
records.what_you_do: Join the Women's or Men's Fellowship for Bible teaching and fellowship, help with clothing and household giveaways or the Safe House Pantry, or give through the donate button on the site.

first_step.how: Call 1-800-543-5244 or email sfwcenter@gmail.com to ask about worship times and how to join a fellowship group.
first_step.basis: The site lists a phone number, an email address, and fellowship groups, but does not give service times or a newcomer program.

records.notes: Legal name: Sanctuary Fellowship Worship Center and Beacon House Ministries. Beacon House is organized under the church, per the site. The batch website was an email address, so the group's own site was found (sfwcenter.com, same name and address). Service days and times are not on the site, so none are written. The site has no dated items, so status is probably_active. Faith is coded protestant because the site says non-denominational and Bible-believing; the owner may want to check. A 2016 Idealist listing appeared in search but was not used, since Idealist is a lead source only.

records.name: SAS Project
records.summary: Gives away gender-affirming clothing for free to trans and queer adults, and offers community care and mutual aid.
records.what_you_do: Donate through the Givebutter or GoFundMe pages, team up on a collaboration or event, or sign up for the monthly newsletter.

first_step.how: Open the Get Support page on sasproject.org to learn how to ask for clothing, or sign up for the monthly newsletter.
first_step.basis: The site has public support and newsletter sign-ups, but it does not describe the steps to get clothing or to volunteer.

records.notes: Full name: Sisters Affirming Sisterhood Project. The site has no dated items. The year 2025 appears only in an image file name, so it was not used. The site does not name Philadelphia or show a street address, so no location is written. The IRS address is 3675 Market St, Philadelphia. The site says it works in six cities, so confirm local service before the owner relies on this record. The summary covers only what the site describes.

records.name: STEM Equity Alliance
records.notes: The site describes work with schools, colleges, and organizations on planning, professional learning for educators, and technical help. It lists no public classes, events, volunteering, or membership; its calls to action are Work with us and Partner with us. Treated as a service provider, not a group a visitor can join. The menu items Teach STEM in PA and Programs and Services were not read. The only date on the page is a 2026 copyright, which is not counted.

records.name: Studio Ludo
records.notes: The site presents play design and research work, including a playground project in Omaha, Nebraska, with pages for presentations, resources, and press. It lists no classes, events, volunteering, or membership, so it reads as a design and research studio rather than a joinable group. Its Our Resources page is a shared folder, not a way in. The only dated text is a 2025 copyright line, which is not counted.

records.name: The Why Project
records.summary: A Philadelphia group that runs summer studios where people make media and animation, plus math and language arts programs built around making things.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for a summer media or animation studio, a math through building program, or an English and language arts in animation program. You can also volunteer through the Volunteer page.

schedule.text: Summer studios in media and animation. Dates are not shown on the page.

first_step.how: Fill out the Program Sign-Up form on thewhyproject.org, or email info@thewhyproject.org to ask about the next summer studio.
first_step.basis: There is a public sign-up page and a volunteer page, but the site gives no dates, costs, or eligibility for the programs.

records.notes: The site has no dated items, so status is probably_active. Ages and costs for the programs are not on the page. No social media links are shown on the page read.

records.name: There's Hope
records.summary: A volunteer group in Philadelphia that helps people in the community, with a volunteer section and an events calendar on its website.
records.what_you_do: Sign up through the Volunteer section of the website, or message the group on Instagram to ask how to help.

first_step.how: Open the Volunteer section on theresh0pe.org, or message the group on Instagram, to ask how to sign up.
first_step.basis: A volunteer section exists, but the page read did not give the steps to sign up.

records.notes: Legal name: There S Hope Association. The site names HopeForPhilly.org as its web address; that domain did not resolve on two tries, so the batch website was read. The footer copyright of 2024 is not counted. The calendar section shows no events on the page read, and the Volunteer, Calendar, and About pages were not read. The IRS address is 415 S 56th Street; the site does not publish one, so it is not written here.

records.name: Transformation CDC
records.summary: A community development group in Mantua that serves meals through its Bread 4 Life program and helps high school seniors with college applications.
records.what_you_do: Ask about Bread 4 Life meals, which a testimonial on the site says run on Tuesdays. Ask about the education mentorship, which helps seniors build college admission portfolios and apply.

schedule.text: Bread 4 Life meals on Tuesdays, per a resident testimonial on the site

first_step.how: Use the Contact Us form on transformcdc.org to ask about Bread 4 Life meal times or to start the college mentorship.
first_step.basis: Meals and mentorship are described, but the site gives no sign-up steps, hours, or eligibility.

records.notes: Legal name: Transformation Community Development Corporation. The footer copyright of 2023 is not counted. The site has no dated items. The Community Engagement section repeats the mission text without program details, and the Community Events section has images only. The site shows no address, phone, or email, so the IRS address (3732 Fairmount Ave) is not written here.

records.name: Alpha Kappa Psi, Epsilon Rho Chapter
records.notes: Legal name: Trustees of the University of Pennsylvania. Aka on the IRS record: Alpha Kappa Psi Professional Business Fraternity Epsilon Rho Chapter. The website did not resolve (DNS error), so nothing could be read and no summary or categories were written. Both searches were spent on congregations (Righteous Healing, Sanctuary), so this group was not searched. Held back. A later pass with one search could find the chapter's university listing.

records.name: UPLIFT
records.summary: Runs UPLIFT Academy, an early learning school in Philadelphia with a Montessori approach to reading and STEM, and funds reading rooms and meals for children in Liberia.
records.what_you_do: Enroll a child at UPLIFT Academy, ask about volunteering through the contact form, or give to the Hungry No More campaign for meals in Liberia.

first_step.how: Start an enrollment on the Enroll Now page at upliftworld.org, or call 267-226-9748 to ask about UPLIFT Academy.
first_step.basis: The Academy has a public enrollment page and a phone number, but the page gives no tuition or start dates.

records.notes: Legal name: United Peoples Learning Initiative for Tomorrow (aka Uplift). The home page impact counters show 0, so they were not used. No dated items; the 2026 copyright is not counted. Work in Liberia and Mali is listed, but only the Philadelphia Academy is a local way in. Tutoring is the closest tag for an early learning school. The email is printed on the site, though its link there is a placeholder.

records.name: University City Eruv
records.notes: Legal name: University City Eruv Corporation. The old domain redirects to pennocp.org/eruv, which was read. The eruv is a religious boundary kept up by the corporation, with weekly checks by student volunteers. The page lists officers and a donation link but no way to volunteer, join, or contact the corporation, so it counts as no public way in. Whether the eruv itself belongs in the directory as infrastructure is for the owner to decide. The page says the corporation is not affiliated with Penn OCP; the footer names Orthodox Community at Penn.

notes: 15 groups. Searches: 2 of 2 used, both on the two congregations whose website field was an email address (Righteous Healing found no page; Sanctuary Fellowship led to its own site, sfwcenter.com, which was then fetched). Fetches: 18 calls. Verdict counts: 12 publish (9 with full content, 3 held back as unknown: Righteous Healing Ministries, Roboracer Foundation, Alpha Kappa Psi Epsilon Rho Chapter), 2 not_a_group (STEM Equity Alliance, Studio Ludo), 1 hide (University City Eruv, private). Most statuses are probably_active because the sites show no dated items; copyright footers were not counted as evidence. The Penn AKPsi and Roboracer domains were not searched because the search budget was spent. The eruv old domain redirected to pennocp.org/eruv, which was read as the group's page. Leads not added: Penn Hillel, Meor Penn, and Chabad at Penn (named on the eruv page), Toys for Tots (named on the MLK site), and the Safe House Pantry (named on the Sanctuary site) were named but not checked, and campus, national, or pantry names are left for a later pass. The Idealist listing for Sanctuary was seen only in search and was not used as a fact source.
